subject: Using distance data to measure habitat selection

messages.author: 5573f844f14103fb
messages.subject: Using distance data to measure habitat selection
parts:
Dear Group 

I have a dataset of gazelle locations sampled using a systematic line transect distance survey of a 220km2 area. I calculated density and abundance using the Distance software and would now like to understand what factors are involved in the observed gazelle distribution. I understand I can use habitat covariates using using distance software, but thought a better way would be to create a resource selection function using the gazelle point data and a used / available design. I read two papers that did this some time ago by Brian Manly (2002) and L. Kastdalen (2003), but have not seen the method used since then, which makes me suspicious that I am missing something. Is there any reason why I should not use this method for data collected during distance surveys?   

Appreciate any thoughts about this. best wishes, Steve

Method for gaining available sample (Kastdalen et al. 2003)
To correct for the unequal detection of gazelle according to distance from the observer, we created a random selection of available points using ArcGIS within a 500m buffer from the transect lines, indicating the cut point from the detection probability function. For each random point generated we then estimated the probability that it should be sampled according to the detection probability function for the lines. 

Kastdalen, L., Pedersen, H. C., Fjone, G., & Andreassen, H. P. (2003). Combining resource selection functions and distance sampling: an example with willow ptarmigan. Proceedings of 1st International Conference on Resource Selection by Animals, Laramie, Wyoming.

 

Manly, B. F. (2002). Estimating a resource selection function with line transect sampling. Journal of Applied Mathematics and Decision Sciences, 6(4), 213-228.

Best regards,
